title: The garden
hook: what no eye has seen or ear heard

segments.voice: Yesterday, the fire, and your line: turn back in time. Did you give something small to someone? Today, the other side of the picture. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-four.

Try describing the color red to someone who has never seen color. You can say warm, you can say fire, you can say the inside of a pomegranate. Every word points, and none of them arrives. The Qur'an describes the garden of paradise with rivers, shade, fruit, and peace. And then the tradition does something unexpected. It says, in effect: whatever you're picturing, it's more than that. Today, the garden, and a sentence about what no one has seen.
screen: `RED, TO SOMEONE WHO NEVER SAW COLOR.` → `RIVERS, SHADE, FRUIT.` → `MORE THAN THAT.`

segments.voice: The Arabic word is jannah, a garden, and the Qur'an pictures it in many passages: gardens with rivers flowing beneath, shade that doesn't fade, fruit within reach, and greetings of peace. Then comes today's hadith. It's a hadith qudsi, a saying the Prophet, peace be upon him, reports from Allah. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has never occurred to a human heart. Three doors, and all three closed. The eye can't reach it. The ear can't reach it. Even imagination can't reach it. In the same report, the companion Abu Hurayrah adds: recite, if you like, this verse. And the verse, in Pickthall's translation, is this: "No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do." Kept hid. So the descriptions in the Qur'an are real, and Muslims take them seriously, but they're also signposts. They point at a joy bigger than the pointing. Scholars have discussed how literally to read the garden's details, and they've answered in more than one way. But this hadith keeps everyone humble. Whatever your picture is, it's smaller than the thing. What does that do in a life? It changes how the garden works. It isn't a catalog to be calculated. It's a hope that stays open, and a reminder that the best joy you've tasted is a hint, not the whole.
screen: `JANNAH: A GARDEN WITH RIVERS.` · `NO EYE, NO EAR, NO HEART.` · `KEPT HID: A JOY BEYOND THE PICTURE.` · then, large: `A HINT, NOT THE WHOLE.`

segments.voice: The practice: imagine joy. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one moment of real joy you've had. A laugh at a kitchen table, cool water on a hot day, someone's face lighting up when they saw you. Let it fill in: the light, the sounds, the feeling in your chest. Stay there for a few breaths. Then, gently, hold the hadith next to it: no eye has seen, no ear has heard. Let your joy be a hint pointing past itself. If you pray, you can thank Allah for that moment with alhamdulillah. If not, just let it be a thank-you. The bell holds the time.
The garden. Jannah: paradise in the Qur'an, rivers and shade and peace, and in the hadith, a joy that no eye has seen and no heart has imagined. Today's word.
Your line: no eye has seen. Today, when something good happens, let it be a hint of more. Tomorrow, seeing Him. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims affirm the garden (jannah) as part of belief in the Last Day; teachers often pair the Qur'an's descriptions with the hadith qudsi that it holds what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined.
